1	\section{Method}
2	\label{sec:method}
3	
4	\begin{figure}[t]
5	\centering
6	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/pipeline.pdf}
7	\caption{Overview of the generational depth estimation pipeline. Seed documents from C4 are recursively passed through a generation operator $G_\delta$ to produce a depth chain $X \to Y_1 \to \cdots \to Y_K$. Statistical features extracted by an external scorer model are fed to the OBD-LightGBM classifier for depth prediction.}
8	\label{fig:pipeline}
9	\end{figure}
10	
11	\subsection{Problem Formulation}
12	\label{sec:formulation}
13	
14	Recursive text generation naturally forms an iterated lossy channel.
15	Let $X$ denote an original human-written document drawn from a source distribution $\mathcal{D}$.
16	A generation operator $G_\delta = \text{LLM} + \delta$, parameterized by a decoding strategy $\delta$ (e.g., nucleus sampling with top-$p$ and temperature $T$), produces successive generations:
17	\begin{equation}
18	  X \to Y_1 \to Y_2 \to \cdots \to Y_K, \quad Y_k = G_\delta(Y_{k-1}),
19	  \label{eq:markov}
20	\end{equation}
21	where $Y_0 \triangleq X$.
22	The sequence $\{Y_k\}_{k=0}^K$ forms a Markov chain, since each generation depends only on its immediate predecessor.
23	
24	By the Data Processing Inequality (DPI), mutual information between the original document and successive generations is monotonically non-increasing:
25	\begin{equation}
26	  I(X; Y_1) \geq I(X; Y_2) \geq \cdots \geq 0.
27	  \label{eq:dpi}
28	\end{equation}
29	Since mutual information is bounded below by zero, this monotone sequence converges: the original signal degrades monotonically across generations.
30	Moreover, when the generation operator defines a finite-state Markov chain, the marginal distributions of adjacent generations converge to a shared stationary distribution, so that any classifier's ability to distinguish depth $k$ from depth $k{+}1$ must eventually degrade to chance.
31	Together, these arguments guarantee the existence of a finite $\Ktheory$ beyond which adjacent generations are indistinguishable---the \emph{information-theoretic discrimination boundary}.
32	
33	Motivated by this theoretical guarantee, we set out to \emph{empirically measure} the discrimination boundary.
34	We define an operational lower bound $\Kempirical$ via a classifier's ability to distinguish adjacent generations:
35	\begin{equation}
36	  \Kempirical = \max\{k : \text{CI}_{\text{lower}}^{95\%}(\auc_{k,k+1}) > \theta\},
37	  \label{eq:kstar}
38	\end{equation}
39	where $\auc_{k,k+1}$ is the pairwise area under the ROC curve for distinguishing depth $k$ from $k{+}1$, $\text{CI}_{\text{lower}}^{95\%}$ denotes the lower bound of a bootstrap 95\% confidence interval (1{,}000 resamples), and $\theta$ is an operational threshold justified in \S\ref{sec:kstar_operational}.
40	Since any specific classifier can only recover a subset of the information-theoretically available signal, $\Kempirical \leq \Ktheory$ by construction.
41	
42	\subsection{Feature Extraction}
43	\label{sec:features}
44	
45	We characterize each document with a 15-dimensional statistical feature vector, organized into four groups (Table~\ref{tab:features}).
46	All features are computed from token-level surprisal values and frequency statistics obtained via an external scorer model on the tokenized text.
47	
48	\begin{table}[t]
49	\centering
50	\small
51	\caption{The 15-dimensional feature set for generational depth estimation.}
52	\label{tab:features}
53	\begin{tabular}{lll}
54	\toprule
55	\textbf{Group} & \textbf{Feature} & \textbf{Description} \\
56	\midrule
57	\multirow{4}{*}{\parbox{2.2cm}{Surprisal\\moments}}
58	  & \texttt{surp\_mean}      & Mean token surprisal \\
59	  & \texttt{surp\_std}       & Std.\ dev.\ of token surprisal \\
60	  & \texttt{surp\_skew}      & Skewness of surprisal dist. \\
61	  & \texttt{surp\_kurt}      & Kurtosis of surprisal dist. \\
62	\midrule
63	\multirow{5}{*}{\parbox{2.2cm}{Surprisal\\derivatives}}
64	  & \texttt{surp\_d1\_mean}  & Mean 1st-order surprisal diff. \\
65	  & \texttt{surp\_d1\_std}   & Std.\ dev.\ of 1st-order diff. \\
66	  & \texttt{surp\_d1\_skew}  & Skewness of 1st-order diff. \\
67	  & \texttt{surp\_d2\_mean}  & Mean 2nd-order surprisal diff. \\
68	  & \texttt{surp\_d2\_std}   & Std.\ dev.\ of 2nd-order diff. \\
69	\midrule
70	\multirow{3}{*}{\parbox{2.2cm}{Vocabulary\\diversity}}
71	  & \texttt{ttr}             & Type-token ratio \\
72	  & \texttt{hapax\_ratio}    & Hapax legomena / unique tokens \\
73	  & \texttt{self\_bleu}      & 4-gram self-BLEU (within-document) \\
74	\midrule
75	\multirow{3}{*}{\parbox{2.2cm}{Frequency\\tail}}
76	  & \texttt{freq\_kurtosis}  & Kurtosis of token frequencies \\
77	  & \texttt{freq\_entropy}   & Token frequency entropy \\
78	  & \texttt{low\_freq\_ratio} & Fraction of rare tokens (freq $\leq 2$) \\
79	\bottomrule
80	\end{tabular}
81	\end{table}
82	
83	The first two groups capture the distribution and dynamics of token-level surprisal: moments summarize the shape of the surprisal distribution, while derivatives measure its local variability across token positions.
84	Vocabulary diversity features quantify lexical richness and repetitiveness: type-token ratio and hapax proportion reflect vocabulary breadth, while self-BLEU detects the increased intra-document $n$-gram overlap characteristic of deeper generations.
85	Frequency tail features characterize the token frequency distribution, capturing the well-documented phenomenon whereby recursive generation concentrates probability mass on high-frequency tokens and reduces the fraction of rare tokens \cite{shumailov2024collapse, dohmatob2024model}.
86	
87	We use hand-crafted statistical features rather than learned representations for three reasons: (1) they are directly interpretable, enabling degradation ordering analysis across model families; (2) they transfer across generators without retraining the feature extractor; and (3) they permit attribution of discriminative power to specific text properties, which is essential for understanding \emph{how} the depth signal degrades (full feature definitions in Table~\ref{tab:s5_features}).
88	
89	\subsection{Ordinal Binary Decomposition Classifier}
90	\label{sec:classifier}
91	
92	Generational depth is inherently ordinal: depth~1 is closer to depth~0 than depth~3 is.
93	We exploit this structure via \emph{Ordinal Binary Decomposition} (OBD), which decomposes a $(K{+}1)$-class ordinal classification problem into $K$ cumulative binary sub-classifiers.
94	The $k$-th sub-classifier estimates the exceedance probability:
95	\begin{equation}
96	  P(\text{depth} > k \mid \mathbf{x}), \quad k = 0, 1, \ldots, K{-}1,
97	\end{equation}
98	where $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^{15}$ is the feature vector.
99	Each sub-classifier is an independent LightGBM model (hyperparameters in Table~\ref{tab:s6_lgbm_params}).
100	Class probabilities are recovered via the decomposition $P(Y{=}0) = 1 - P(Y{>}0)$ and $P(Y{=}k) = P(Y{>}k{-}1) - P(Y{>}k)$ for $k \geq 1$.
101	The predicted depth is:
102	\begin{equation}
103	  \hat{d}(\mathbf{x}) = \operatorname*{arg\,max}_{k} \; P(Y{=}k \mid \mathbf{x}).
104	\end{equation}
105	
106	We compared OBD-LightGBM against two alternatives: standard (unordered) multiclass LightGBM and ordinal logistic regression (LogisticAT).
107	OBD-LightGBM achieves lower mean absolute error (MAE) than multiclass LightGBM across all three model families (Qwen-rewrite: 0.984 vs.\ 1.016; Pythia: 1.107 vs.\ 1.140; OLMo: 1.147 vs.\ 1.181).
108	Ordinal logistic regression yields the lowest MAE overall (e.g., 0.911 on Qwen-rewrite) but at the cost of substantially degraded pairwise discrimination: mean pairwise $\auc$ of 0.4883 versus 0.6095 for OBD-LightGBM, averaged across the three families.
109	The low MAE of ordinal logistic regression stems from collapsing predictions toward central depths rather than improved discrimination---a pathology that renders it unsuitable when pairwise depth discriminability is the primary objective.
110	
111	\subsection{Operationalizing $\Kstar$}
112	\label{sec:kstar_operational}
113	
114	We set the operational threshold at $\theta = 0.60$.
115	This choice is grounded in the permutation test null distribution: across all model configurations, the 95th percentile of the null $\auc$ (obtained from 500 random label permutations) falls below 0.55.
116	A threshold of $\theta = 0.60$ therefore requires classification performance that is statistically significantly above chance at the $\alpha = 0.05$ level.
117	
118	Uncertainty is quantified via bootstrap resampling (1{,}000 resamples) of $\auc_{k,k+1}$ for each adjacent depth pair.
119	$\Kempirical$ is defined as the maximum depth $k$ for which $\text{CI}_{\text{lower}}^{95\%}(\auc_{k,k+1}) > \theta$ (Eq.~\ref{eq:kstar}).
120	
121	We examine threshold sensitivity at $\theta \in \{0.55, 0.60, 0.65, 0.70\}$.
122	At $\theta = 0.60$, $\Kempirical = 2$ holds across all four model configurations, with all permutation $p$-values for depth pair $1$ vs.\ $2$ at $p = 0.002$.
123	At the more lenient $\theta = 0.55$, $\Kempirical = 3$ uniformly across all four configurations.
124	At the stricter $\theta = 0.65$, only the rewrite configuration retains $\Kempirical = 2$; continuation-mode configurations yield $\Kempirical = 1$.
125	At $\theta = 0.70$, $\Kempirical = 1$ across all configurations.
126	This sensitivity profile confirms that $\Kempirical = 2$ is robust at our chosen threshold while remaining appropriately responsive to more stringent criteria.
127	
128	\subsection{Experimental Setup}
129	\label{sec:experimental_setup}
130	
131	We evaluate four model configurations spanning three model families and two generation modes (Table~\ref{tab:setup}).
132	
133	\begin{table}[t]
134	\centering
135	\small
136	\caption{Experimental configurations. All use the same seed corpus and evaluation protocol (5-fold group cross-validation grouped by seed document, $\auc$ as primary metric).}
137	\label{tab:setup}
138	\begin{tabular}{llcccc}
139	\toprule
140	\textbf{Config} & \textbf{Model} & \textbf{Mode} & \textbf{Decoding} & $N$ & \textbf{Depth} \\
141	\midrule
142	Qwen-rw   & Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct & Rewrite      & $p{=}0.95$, $T{=}1.0$ & 5{,}000 & 0--5 \\
143	Qwen-cont & Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct & Continuation & $p{=}0.95$, $T{=}1.0$ & 5{,}000 & 0--5 \\
144	Pythia    & Pythia-1.4B            & Continuation & $p{=}0.95$, $T{=}1.0$ & 5{,}000 & 0--5 \\
145	OLMo      & OLMo-1B               & Continuation & $p{=}0.95$, $T{=}1.0$ & 5{,}000 & 0--5 \\
146	\bottomrule
147	\end{tabular}
148	\end{table}
149	
150	\paragraph{Seed corpus.}
151	We sample 5{,}000 documents from the C4 validation split, each truncated to 256 tokens, providing a controlled and reproducible starting point.
152	
153	\paragraph{Depth chain.}
154	Each seed document is recursively passed through the generation operator for $K = 5$ iterations, producing depths 0 (original) through 5.
155	This yields 30{,}000 documents per configuration (5{,}000 seeds $\times$ 6 depth levels).
156	
157	\paragraph{Decoding.}
158	All configurations use nucleus sampling with $p = 0.95$ and temperature $T = 1.0$, which we treat as the standard decoding condition.
159	The effect of alternative decoding strategies (greedy, lower temperature, different $p$) on $\Kempirical$ is examined in a separate ablation (\S\ref{sec:experiments}).
160	
161	\paragraph{Evaluation.}
162	We report pairwise $\auc$ for each adjacent depth pair $(k, k{+}1)$ under 5-fold group cross-validation (grouped by seed document to prevent cross-depth leakage), with bootstrap 95\% confidence intervals.
163	Ordinal MAE and Kendall's $\tau_b$ are reported as secondary metrics.
164	Dataset statistics are provided in Table~\ref{tab:s4_dataset_stats}; per-fold bootstrap results in Table~\ref{tab:s8_cv_folds}.
165	
166	\subsection{Generation Mode Control}
167	\label{sec:generation_mode_method}
168	
169	We investigate two generation modes that capture distinct recursive contamination scenarios:
170	
171	\paragraph{Continuation.}
172	The seed document is truncated to its first 128 tokens, and the LLM generates a continuation to 256 tokens.
173	This simulates scenarios where partial human text is extended by a model, a common pattern in collaborative writing and web content generation.
174	
175	\paragraph{Rewrite.}
176	The LLM receives the instruction ``Rewrite the following text while preserving its meaning'' and generates a full paraphrase.
177	This simulates content rewriting pipelines where existing text is rephrased at scale.
178	
179	We designate continuation as the \emph{canonical condition} for cross-model comparisons, based on three empirical findings from the cross-model transfer analysis.
180	First, classifiers trained on continuation-mode data retain 80--92\% accuracy when transferred across model families, versus only 61--63\% for rewrite-mode classifiers.
181	Second, the higher pairwise $\auc$ observed in rewrite mode ($\auc_{1,2} = 0.6955$ vs.\ $0.6112$ for continuation on Qwen) reflects instruction-following style artifacts rather than a stronger intrinsic depth signal, as evidenced by the poor cross-model transfer.
182	Third, the asymmetric transfer---continuation${\to}$rewrite retains 89\% performance versus rewrite${\to}$continuation at 82\%---indicates that continuation-mode features form a generalizable subset of what rewrite-mode classifiers exploit.
183	We therefore report continuation-mode results as primary and treat rewrite-mode results as an upper-bound ablation that quantifies the effect of mode-specific signal amplification.
184

1	\section{Introduction}
2	\label{sec:introduction}
3	
4	Web-scale text corpora are increasingly contaminated by synthetic content that has itself been generated from earlier synthetic content.
5	Each pass through a language model constitutes a lossy channel: first-generation synthetic text retains much of the information structure of its human-written source, but within just two or three generations the output is qualitatively different---tail modes vanish, lexical diversity contracts, and surprisal distributions flatten~\cite{shumailov2024collapse, dohmatob2024model}.
6	This recursive degradation is not merely a theoretical concern; as synthetic text proliferates on the open web, training corpora inevitably ingest documents at varying generational depths, amplifying the risk of model collapse in downstream systems.
7	Yet the dominant paradigm in synthetic text detection treats all machine-generated text identically: a document is classified as human or synthetic, with no regard for how many rounds of recursive generation it has undergone.
8	This binary framing discards the generational depth dimension entirely.
9	
10	The gap cuts across three research communities.
11	Binary detection methods---including DivEye~\cite{basani2026diveye}, Min-K\%++~\cite{zhang2024minkpp}, and CoDeC~\cite{zawalski2026codec}---achieve strong human-versus-machine separation but produce no depth estimate.
12	The model collapse literature provides macro-level characterizations of recursive degradation: Shumailov et al.~\cite{shumailov2024collapse} demonstrated irreversible tail loss, Alemohammad et al.~\cite{alemohammad2024selfconsuming} proved convergence to a fixed point, and Schaeffer et al.~\cite{schaeffer2025position} organized the field into a taxonomy of eight definitions---yet none of these works provides a tool for estimating the generational depth of an individual text.
13	Data selection methods such as DSIR~\cite{xie2023dsir}, D4~\cite{tirumala2023d4}, and DoReMi~\cite{xie2023doremi} perform distribution matching to improve corpus quality but ignore recursive depth altogether.
14	The closest prior work is Drayson et al.~\cite{drayson2025}, who combined binary machine-generated text detection with stratified importance resampling to prevent model collapse---but their approach remains fundamentally binary.
15	No existing method estimates how many rounds of recursive generation a text has undergone, nor quantifies the boundary beyond which such estimation becomes infeasible.
16	
17	Recursive generation forms an iterated lossy channel; the Data Processing Inequality guarantees that the original signal degrades monotonically across generations, motivating the existence of a finite discrimination boundary $\Kstar$ beyond which adjacent generations become indistinguishable.
18	Markov chain convergence further implies that adjacent-generation distributions converge to a shared stationary distribution, so the classifier's task grows harder with each step.
19	Motivated by this theoretical structure, we set out to empirically measure $\Kempirical$---the maximum depth at which a classifier can reliably distinguish adjacent generations.
20	Our approach combines a 15-dimensional statistical feature pipeline---capturing surprisal moments, surprisal derivatives, vocabulary diversity, and frequency tail statistics---with an Ordinal Binary Decomposition (OBD) LightGBM classifier that respects the ordinal structure of depth.
21	We operationalize $\Kempirical$ as the deepest generation at which adjacent depths remain statistically distinguishable, with the bootstrap 95\% CI for pairwise $\auc$ exceeding an operational threshold $\theta = 0.60$ (formal definition in Section~\ref{sec:method}).
22	The choice of interpretable statistical features---rather than learned representations---is deliberate: it enables cross-generator transfer without retraining and permits attribution of discriminative power to specific text properties.
23	
24	Our contributions are organized into two groups.
25	The primary contribution is a systematic empirical characterization of $\Kempirical$ and its properties:
26	
27	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
28	  \item \textbf{$\Kempirical = 2$: a consistent boundary across all tested conditions.}
29	    Across 4 model-mode configurations and 4 decoding strategies (8 conditions total), all 1v2 bootstrap CI lower bounds exceed $\theta = 0.60$ and all 2v3 CI upper bounds fall below $\theta$, with permutation $p \leq 0.002$ for all boundary comparisons.
30	    The most marginal case is Qwen-continuation, where $\text{CI}_\text{lower} = 0.6015$.
31	    $\Kempirical = 2$ is thus established as a consistent discrimination boundary across all 8 tested conditions at the $\leq$1.5B scale.
32	    Higher decoding entropy increases signal strength ($\auc_{1,2}$: $0.69$ greedy $\to$ $0.70$ at $T{=}1.2$) but does not shift the boundary.
33	
34	  \item \textbf{Cross-model transfer.}
35	    Classifiers trained on one continuation-mode model and evaluated on another retain 80--92\% of within-model accuracy (Pythia$\leftrightarrow$OLMo: 90--92\%).
36	    At the 0v1 boundary, cross-model $\auc$ exceeds 0.96 across all tested model pairs.
37	    Transfer retention of 80--92\% suggests a large text-intrinsic component of the depth signal, rather than generator-specific artifacts.
38	
39	  \item \textbf{Degradation ordering consistency.}
40	    Single-feature $\auc$ rankings are highly correlated across continuation-mode models (Spearman $\rho \geq 0.85$), with the same top features---\texttt{surp\_d1\_std}, \texttt{surp\_std}, \texttt{surp\_d2\_std}---appearing across all three families.
41	    This shared ordering suggests a common degradation mechanism: each generation step smooths the token-level surprisal landscape.
42	    A limitation is that depth-pair-level agreement weakens ($\tau \approx 0.37$ at 1v2), indicating that individual feature contributions at the boundary vary across models.
43	
44	  \item \textbf{Generation mode analysis.}
45	    Within Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, rewrite mode yields 1v2 $\auc = 0.6955$ versus continuation's $0.6112$ ($\Delta = +8.4$\,pp), but rewrite-trained classifiers transfer poorly across models (61--63\% retention versus 80--92\% for continuation).
46	    Cross-mode transfer is asymmetric: continuation$\to$rewrite retains 89\% while rewrite$\to$continuation retains 82\%.
47	    Continuation mode is therefore recommended as the canonical condition for cross-model comparisons.
48	\end{enumerate}
49	
50	\noindent As a secondary contribution, we investigate whether the coarse 3-class ordinal signal implied by $\Kempirical = 2$ enables \emph{graduated filtering}---depth-aware data curation that preserves mildly contaminated text (depth~1, retaining most original signal) while removing deeply corrupted text (depth~$\geq 2$)---and whether such filtering can improve upon binary approaches that discard all synthetic content indiscriminately (Section~\ref{sec:experiments}).
51	
52	The remainder of this paper is organized as follows.
53	Section~\ref{sec:related_work} reviews related work.
54	Section~\ref{sec:method} describes the method.
55	Section~\ref{sec:experiments} presents experimental results.
56	Section~\ref{sec:discussion} discusses implications and limitations.
57	Section~\ref{sec:conclusion} concludes.

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Web-scale text corpora are increasingly contaminated by synthetic content that has itself been generated from earlier synthetic content.
Each pass through a language model constitutes a lossy channel: first-generation synthetic text retains much of the information structure of its human-written source, but within just two or three generations the output is qualitatively different---tail modes vanish, lexical diversity contracts, and surprisal distributions flatten~\cite{shumailov2024collapse, dohmatob2024model}.
This recursive degradation is not merely a theoretical concern; as synthetic text proliferates on the open web, training corpora inevitably ingest documents at varying generational depths, amplifying the risk of model collapse in downstream systems.
Yet the dominant paradigm in synthetic text detection treats all machine-generated text identically: a document is classified as human or synthetic, with no regard for how many rounds of recursive generation it has undergone.
This binary framing discards the generational depth dimension entirely.

The gap cuts across three research communities.
Binary detection methods---including DivEye~\cite{basani2026diveye}, Min-K\%++~\cite{zhang2024minkpp}, and CoDeC~\cite{zawalski2026codec}---achieve strong human-versus-machine separation but produce no depth estimate.
The model collapse literature provides macro-level characterizations of recursive degradation: Shumailov et al.~\cite{shumailov2024collapse} demonstrated irreversible tail loss, Alemohammad et al.~\cite{alemohammad2024selfconsuming} proved convergence to a fixed point, and Schaeffer et al.~\cite{schaeffer2025position} organized the field into a taxonomy of eight definitions---yet none of these works provides a tool for estimating the generational depth of an individual text.
Data selection methods such as DSIR~\cite{xie2023dsir}, D4~\cite{tirumala2023d4}, and DoReMi~\cite{xie2023doremi} perform distribution matching to improve corpus quality but ignore recursive depth altogether.
The closest prior work is Drayson et al.~\cite{drayson2025}, who combined binary machine-generated text detection with stratified importance resampling to prevent model collapse---but their approach remains fundamentally binary.
No existing method estimates how many rounds of recursive generation a text has undergone, nor quantifies the boundary beyond which such estimation becomes infeasible.

Recursive generation forms an iterated lossy channel; the Data Processing Inequality guarantees that the original signal degrades monotonically across generations, motivating the existence of a finite discrimination boundary $\Kstar$ beyond which adjacent generations become indistinguishable.
Markov chain convergence further implies that adjacent-generation distributions converge to a shared stationary distribution, so the classifier's task grows harder with each step.
Motivated by this theoretical structure, we set out to empirically measure $\Kempirical$---the maximum depth at which a classifier can reliably distinguish adjacent generations.
Our approach combines a 15-dimensional statistical feature pipeline---capturing surprisal moments, surprisal derivatives, vocabulary diversity, and frequency tail statistics---with an Ordinal Binary Decomposition (OBD) LightGBM classifier that respects the ordinal structure of depth.
We operationalize $\Kempirical$ as the deepest generation at which adjacent depths remain statistically distinguishable, with the bootstrap 95\% CI for pairwise $\auc$ exceeding an operational threshold $\theta = 0.60$ (formal definition in Section~\ref{sec:method}).
The choice of interpretable statistical features---rather than learned representations---is deliberate: it enables cross-generator transfer without retraining and permits attribution of discriminative power to specific text properties.

Our contributions are organized into two groups.
The primary contribution is a systematic empirical characterization of $\Kempirical$ and its properties:

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
  \item \textbf{$\Kempirical = 2$: a consistent boundary across all tested conditions.}
    Across 4 model-mode configurations and 4 decoding strategies (8 conditions total), all 1v2 bootstrap CI lower bounds exceed $\theta = 0.60$ and all 2v3 CI upper bounds fall below $\theta$, with permutation $p \leq 0.002$ for all boundary comparisons.
    The most marginal case is Qwen-continuation, where $\text{CI}_\text{lower} = 0.6015$.
    $\Kempirical = 2$ is thus established as a consistent discrimination boundary across all 8 tested conditions at the $\leq$1.5B scale.
    Higher decoding entropy increases signal strength ($\auc_{1,2}$: $0.69$ greedy $\to$ $0.70$ at $T{=}1.2$) but does not shift the boundary.

  \item \textbf{Cross-model transfer.}
    Classifiers trained on one continuation-mode model and evaluated on another retain 80--92\% of within-model accuracy (Pythia$\leftrightarrow$OLMo: 90--92\%).
    At the 0v1 boundary, cross-model $\auc$ exceeds 0.96 across all tested model pairs.
    Transfer retention of 80--92\% suggests a large text-intrinsic component of the depth signal, rather than generator-specific artifacts.

  \item \textbf{Degradation ordering consistency.}
    Single-feature $\auc$ rankings are highly correlated across continuation-mode models (Spearman $\rho \geq 0.85$), with the same top features---\texttt{surp\_d1\_std}, \texttt{surp\_std}, \texttt{surp\_d2\_std}---appearing across all three families.
    This shared ordering suggests a common degradation mechanism: each generation step smooths the token-level surprisal landscape.
    A limitation is that depth-pair-level agreement weakens ($\tau \approx 0.37$ at 1v2), indicating that individual feature contributions at the boundary vary across models.

  \item \textbf{Generation mode analysis.}
    Within Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, rewrite mode yields 1v2 $\auc = 0.6955$ versus continuation's $0.6112$ ($\Delta = +8.4$\,pp), but rewrite-trained classifiers transfer poorly across models (61--63\% retention versus 80--92\% for continuation).
    Cross-mode transfer is asymmetric: continuation$\to$rewrite retains 89\% while rewrite$\to$continuation retains 82\%.
    Continuation mode is therefore recommended as the canonical condition for cross-model comparisons.
\end{enumerate}

\noindent As a secondary contribution, we investigate whether the coarse 3-class ordinal signal implied by $\Kempirical = 2$ enables \emph{graduated filtering}---depth-aware data curation that preserves mildly contaminated text (depth~1, retaining most original signal) while removing deeply corrupted text (depth~$\geq 2$)---and whether such filtering can improve upon binary approaches that discard all synthetic content indiscriminately (Section~\ref{sec:experiments}).

The remainder of this paper is organized as follows.
Section~\ref{sec:related_work} reviews related work.
Section~\ref{sec:method} describes the method.
Section~\ref{sec:experiments} presents experimental results.
Section~\ref{sec:discussion} discusses implications and limitations.
Section~\ref{sec:conclusion} concludes.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   I am the independent Reviewer for the "gen-depth-contamination" project, an ML research project measuring K* (generational depth discrimination boundary) in recursive synthetic text. My role is to audit experiment conclusions, review paper writing, and post findings to the Director via `reviewer_post_to_director`. I respond in Chinese. The project targets EMNLP 2026 ARR submission on May 25, 2026.

   The conversation involved reviewing multiple worker outputs (C3 fallback outline, reviewer fixes, related work update, neural probe polish, discussion-conclusion polish, exp-006 handoff check), conducting a ROADMAP review, and most recently being asked to perform a comprehensive macro-level paper quality assessment focusing on: (1) claim strength vs evidence, (2) story self-consistency, (3) ablation gaps, (4) related work differentiation — with output of top-3 actionable suggestions ranked by impact/cost.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - K* (K-star): generational depth discrimination boundary — the maximum depth at which adjacent generations are statistically distinguishable
   - K*_empirical=2: measured across 8 conditions (4 model-mode configs + 4 decoding strategies) at ≤1.5B scale
   - K*_neural=3: from frozen LLM embeddings + MLP probe (preliminary, single dataset Qwen-cont only)
   - K*_theory ≥ K*_neural ≥ K*_15D hierarchy
   - θ=0.60 operational threshold for K* determination via bootstrap 95% CI lower bound
   - OBD (Ordinal Binary Decomposition): LightGBM classifier respecting ordinal depth structure
   - 15-dimensional statistical feature set: surprisal moments, surprisal derivatives, vocabulary diversity, frequency tail
   - DPI (Data Processing Inequality): theoretical motivation for finite K*
   - Graduated filtering: depth-aware data curation using exp(-α·d̂) weighting
   - Cross-model transfer: 80-92% accuracy retention across continuation-mode models
   - 2+1 claim structure: C1' (K* characterization) + C3 (graduated filtering) + supporting analysis
   - D013 fallback: three narrative tracks (Version A: graduated wins, Version B: binary optimal, Version B2: DSIR wins)

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `ROADMAP.md` — Research dashboard; tracks progress (11 DONE + 1 RUNNING), strategic risks, timeline, GPU budget. Shows C3 intermediate warning and CRITICAL fixes completed.
   - `registry.yaml` — 12 experiments: mvp_pilot_sat_v1, exp_001-003, exp_005-007, exp_010-011, exp_013, exp_015, exp_017 (all DONE), exp_006 (RUNNING 29/50)
   - `paper_framing.md` — Defines 2+1 claim structure, anticipated reviewer concerns (9 listed), venue fit, canonical experimental condition (continuation mode), C1' sub-components (a-e)
   - `decisions.yaml` — D001-D022 decision chain, particularly D013 (C3 fallback), D017 (claim strength), D019-D020 (K*_neural positioning)
   - `artifacts/c3_fallback_outline.md` — Dual-track outline: Version A (graduated wins), Version B (binary optimal with 8-section detail), Version B2 (DSIR wins). Contains table/figure checklist, contingency triggers (p>0.05 + <0.5pp), cross-section impact mapping.
   - `artifacts/c3_contingency_versions.tex` (two copies, synced) — Pre-written LaTeX for Version A and B conclusion/discussion paragraphs. Version B rewritten to use information-theoretic framing after my review.
   - `docs/paper/experiments_c1.tex` (409 lines) — Full experiments section: §4.1 K*=2 across configs (Table kstar_ci, Figure auc_decay), §4.2 Cross-model transfer (Table transfer_matrix), §4.3 Feature degradation ordering, §4.4 Generation mode effect, §4.5 Representation dependence (neural probe with 5 TODO placeholders for exp-015 rerun)
   - `docs/paper/introduction.tex` (57 lines) — Problem statement, gap analysis, DPI motivation, contributions list (a-d enumerated + secondary C3)
   - `docs/paper/method.tex` (184 lines) — Problem formulation (Eq 1-4), 15D feature table, OBD classifier, θ operationalization with sensitivity analysis, experimental setup, generation mode control
   - `docs/paper/discussion.tex` — §5.1 K* representation dependence (lines 28-35 authoritative neural probe), scale considerations (L72-87), LLM zero-shot baseline, decoding strategy discussion, θ-sensitivity, limitations (boundary marginality, operational vs theoretical, feature representation), graduated filtering placeholder
   - `docs/paper/conclusion.tex` (58 lines) — C1' (L6-24), C2 framework (L28-46 with neural probe hedge), C3 placeholder (L48-53 with TODO), limitations (L56), future work (L57)
   - `docs/paper/related_work.tex` (67 lines) — 6 paragraphs: Model Collapse, Binary Detection, Ordinal Classification, Probing Classifiers, Data Selection/Curation, Watermarking. Recently updated with 3 new citations + 2 expansions.
   - `docs/paper/references.bib` — Contains cheng2025beyond, yi2025escaping, mehta2025beyond (new), plus existing entries
   - `artifacts/exp015_neural_probe_results.json` (remote) — Ground truth for neural probe: Qwen-cont only, 2v3 AUC=0.6195 (fold range 0.6052-0.6323), 1v2=0.6983, K*_neural=3, accuracy=0.4335

4. Errors and fixes:
   - `compute_coverage_matrix` tool error: "cannot use 'list' as a dict key (unhashable type: 'list')" — caused by experiments with list-type claim fields in experiment_plan.yaml. Tool bug, worked around by manual coverage analysis.

\section{Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}

% === Contribution 1: K*=2 consistent boundary ===
% Sources: exp_007 (bootstrap CI + permutation), exp_001/exp_002/exp_017/mvp_pilot (model-mode), exp_003 (decoding ablation)
We presented the first systematic measurement of the generational depth
discrimination boundary $\Kempirical$ for recursive synthetic text.
Across three model architectures in four model-mode configurations
(Pythia-1.4B and OLMo-1B in continuation mode; Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct in both
continuation and rewrite modes) and 4 decoding strategies---totaling 8
conditions---we establish $\Kempirical = 2$ as a consistent boundary:
classifiers reliably distinguish adjacent generations up to depth~2, but all
deeper pairs fall below the operational threshold $\theta = 0.60$.
For the four model-mode configurations, bootstrap 95\% confidence intervals
and permutation tests confirm statistical significance at the 1v2 boundary
($p \leq 0.002$ for all four); the most marginal case, Qwen-continuation,
yields a CI lower bound of 0.6015, exceeding $\theta$ by only 0.15\,pp.
All four decoding configurations (greedy, nucleus, $T{=}0.70$, $T{=}1.2$)
likewise yield 1v2 point-estimate $\auc$ above $\theta$.
The 0v1 boundary is near-perfectly separable ($\auc > 0.99$), followed by a
sharp ${\sim}$30\,pp drop at 1v2 ($\auc$: 0.6112--0.7039 across all
conditions), while all 2v3 pairs fall below~$\theta$.
Recursive generation thus acts as a severely lossy channel whose discriminable
statistical fingerprint is exhausted within two steps.

% === Contribution 2: Ordinal depth estimation framework ===
% Sources: exp_010 (OBD vs baselines), exp_013 (cross-model transfer), exp_005 (feature degradation), exp_011 (LLM zero-shot)
To operationalize depth estimation, we introduced an ordinal binary
decomposition (OBD) framework pairing 15 hand-crafted statistical features
with LightGBM classifiers.
Cross-model transfer experiments demonstrate 80--92\% accuracy retention
across continuation-mode model pairs, with
Pythia$\leftrightarrow$OLMo achieving 90--92\% and 0v1 transfer $\auc$
exceeding 0.96 across all tested model pairs---indicating that depth signals are largely
text-intrinsic rather than generator-specific.
Feature degradation orderings are consistent across architectures
(Spearman $\rho \geq 0.85$), with surprisal-variance features dominating
across all tested families, suggesting that the two-step information loss is driven primarily by the
autoregressive mechanism at this scale.
As a reference point, frontier LLMs (GPT-5.5, Claude Opus~4.6) achieve
${\sim}$88\% binary human-vs.-synthetic accuracy but only ${\sim}$33\% on
5-class depth estimation, below OBD-LightGBM's 38.6\%---confirming that
fine-grained depth discrimination requires specialized statistical features
rather than general language understanding.
A preliminary neural probing experiment suggests that this operational bound is not tight: a frozen Qwen2.5-1.5B encoder paired with an MLP classifier achieves $\Kempirical^{\text{neural}} = 3$ on the Qwen-continuation dataset (2v3 $\auc = 0.6195$ versus 0.5609 with hand-crafted features), indicating that learned representations recover depth signal beyond the 15-dimensional feature set.
This result, pending cross-model validation, provides initial evidence that $\Ktheory \geq 3$.

% === Contribution 3: Graduated filtering (C3) ===
% Source: exp_006 (RUNNING — results pending)
The $\Kempirical = 2$ boundary implies a natural trichotomy---human (depth~0), first-generation synthetic (depth~1), and deeper synthetic (depth~$\geq 2$)---that can be exploited for depth-aware data curation.
% TODO: exp-006 graduated filtering 具体结果填充。
% 预留内容：graduated filtering 利用三级分类法在 MMLU/HellaSwag 上的表现，
% 与 binary filtering 和 no-filter baseline 的对比。

% === Limitations + Future Work ===
Our findings are bounded by the scale of models tested ($\leq$1.5B parameters), restriction to English C4 text, and the use of prompt-chain rather than retrain-chain protocols; $\Kempirical$ depends on the threshold $\theta$ and shifts with generation mode (continuation-mode configurations drop to $\Kempirical{=}1$ at $\theta{=}0.65$, while rewrite mode retains $\Kempirical{=}2$; Section~\ref{sec:limitations}); the 15-dimensional feature set yields $\Kempirical$ as an operational lower bound, and $\Ktheory$ may be strictly higher.
Several directions merit investigation: scaling to larger models (7B+) to test whether increased generation fidelity shifts the boundary; extending to multilingual and multi-domain corpora; establishing the relationship between prompt-chain and retrain-chain $\Kstar$ values, which would connect our measurements to the model collapse setting; incorporating few-shot or chain-of-thought prompting for LLM-based depth estimation; and extending the neural probe approach---which has yielded preliminary evidence of $\Kempirical^{\text{neural}} = 3$ on one dataset---through cross-model validation (Pythia, OLMo), bootstrap confidence intervals, multi-layer probing beyond the last hidden state, and comparison with fine-tuned (non-frozen) encoders to further narrow the gap between $\Kempirical$ and $\Ktheory$.

\section{Related Work}
\label{sec:related_work}

\paragraph{Model Collapse and Recursive Generation.}
Training on model-generated data can cause progressive distribution shift known as \emph{model collapse}.
Shumailov et al.~\cite{shumailov2024collapse} showed that iteratively training language models on their own outputs leads to irreversible tail-distribution degradation, with minority modes vanishing across generations.
Alemohammad et al.~\cite{alemohammad2024selfconsuming} formalized this for self-consuming generative models, proving convergence to a fixed point under mild regularity conditions.
Dohmatob et al.~\cite{dohmatob2024model} derived scaling laws for collapse, demonstrating that tail probability mass is lost at rates predictable from model and data scale.
Further work shows that even a vanishingly small fraction of synthetic data suffices to trigger collapse, with the effect amplified in larger models~\citep{dohmatob2025strong}; their distribution-shift analysis and our information-theoretic derivation of $\Kstar$ arrive at the same conclusion from complementary starting points---recursive generation inevitably degrades information to a finite boundary.
Schaeffer et al.~\cite{schaeffer2025position} organized the fragmented literature into a taxonomy of eight definitions across three families.
Our $\Kstar$ aligns with their Family~B (distributional deformation), specifically D4 (collapsing variance) and D6 (mode entanglement)---the features that degrade most rapidly in our experiments are precisely variance-based surprisal measures.
Kazdan et al.~\cite{kazdan2025collapse} distinguished \emph{replace} and \emph{accumulate} regimes: in the replace regime each generation completely supplants its predecessor, producing faster collapse.
Our prompt-chain protocol operates in the replace regime, so $\Kempirical = 2$ is a conservative lower bound; the accumulate regime would yield slower degradation and higher $\Kstar$.
Shi et al.~\cite{shi2025generalization} identified a generalization-to-memorization transition in recursively trained models, providing cross-modal evidence that information loss is progressive.
Gerstgrasser et al.~\cite{gerstgrasser2024inevitable} proved that collapse is avoidable when sufficient original data is retained alongside synthetic samples, a condition that depth-aware curation can enforce by construction.
These works characterize the macro dynamics of collapse but do not provide tools for per-text generational depth estimation.

\paragraph{Binary Synthetic Text Detection.}
Distinguishing machine-generated from human-written text is a well-studied binary classification problem.
Early statistical approaches such as GLTR~\cite{gehrmann2019gltr} visualized per-token likelihood ranks to help human annotators spot generated text, establishing that token-level distributional cues are informative for detection.
Zellers et al.~\cite{zellers2019grover} demonstrated that the generating model itself is an effective detector, while Ippolito et al.~\cite{ippolito2020detection} analyzed how detection difficulty scales with generation quality.
Recent zero-shot methods have narrowed the gap: Mitchell et al.~\cite{mitchell2023detectgpt} introduced DetectGPT, which uses probability curvature to detect machine-generated text without access to the generating model.
Fast-DetectGPT~\citep{bao2024fast} dramatically accelerates this approach via conditional probability curvature, achieving a 340$\times$ speedup with improved accuracy.
Hans et al.~\cite{hans2024binoculars} proposed Binoculars, which computes the cross-perplexity ratio between two closely related language models to achieve near-perfect detection without any training data.
DivEye~\cite{basani2026diveye} uses surprisal diversity features to detect synthetic text without generator-specific training data; their surprisal diversity features overlap with the \texttt{surp\_*} subset of our 15-dimensional feature set, but DivEye optimizes for binary detection whereas our features target ordinal depth discrimination---the same feature family serving tasks at different granularities.
Min-K\%++~\cite{zhang2024minkpp} adapts membership inference techniques to flag model-generated passages via outlier token likelihoods.
CoDeC~\cite{zawalski2026codec} frames contamination detection as in-context learning, calibrating thresholds from few-shot exemplars.

All these methods produce binary outputs and do not distinguish generational depth.
The connection to membership inference is instructive: Min-K\%++ and related approaches test whether a text appeared in training data---a related but distinct question from how many recursive generation steps it has undergone.
A further limitation is that binary detectors cannot separate beneficial recursive generation (e.g., self-refinement, where a model iteratively improves its own output) from harmful recursive contamination, creating systematic false positives when applied to curated synthetic data.
Binary features are designed for the human-vs.-synthetic boundary and are not expected to capture fine-grained depth differences, as the distributional shift between adjacent generations is orders of magnitude smaller than the shift between human and first-generation text.
Recent work moves beyond binary labels along other axes: \cite{cheng2025beyond} measure the degree of human--LLM collaboration, and \cite{mehta2025beyond} propose hierarchical contamination detection across four levels (none/paraphrase/synthetic/memorized).
Both pursue finer-grained characterization of synthetic text but along orthogonal dimensions---collaboration intensity and contamination type, respectively---whereas our depth axis captures recursive generation steps, a complementary facet that neither framework addresses.

\paragraph{Ordinal Classification.}
Ordinal regression methods exploit the natural ordering among class labels to improve generalization over nominal classifiers.
Cao et al.~\cite{cao2020coral} introduced CORAL, which enforces rank consistency through weight sharing in the output layer, guaranteeing that predicted cumulative probabilities are monotonically non-increasing.
Ordinal approaches have been applied in NLP tasks such as sentiment intensity prediction and essay scoring, where adjacent categories share more semantic overlap than distant ones.
Generational depth exhibits the same ordinal structure: text at depth~$k$ is distributionally closer to depth~$k\!\pm\!1$ than to depth~$k\!\pm\!3$, because each recursive generation step introduces an incremental distributional shift rather than a discontinuous one.
Despite this natural fit, ordinal classification has not been applied to synthetic text depth estimation.
The idea of decomposing ordinal problems into a series of binary decisions dates to Frank \& Hall~\cite{frank2001ordinal}; our Ordinal Binary Decomposition (OBD) head follows this principle by learning $K\!-\!1$ cumulative boundary classifiers, yielding monotonic depth predictions and stronger calibration than a flat softmax baseline.

\paragraph{Probing Classifiers.}
Linear and shallow MLP probes have become a standard tool for analyzing what information is encoded in pretrained representations~\cite{alain2017understanding,conneau2018probing}.
Belinkov~\cite{belinkov2022probing} surveys the methodology and cautions that probe complexity must be controlled to ensure that performance reflects representational content rather than probe capacity.
Our neural probe experiment follows this protocol: a two-layer MLP on frozen Qwen2.5-1.5B embeddings, where the probe's limited capacity ensures that discriminability reflects depth information already present in the representations rather than learned de novo.

\paragraph{Data Selection and Curation.}
Principled data selection methods improve training corpus quality through distribution matching and deduplication.
DSIR~\cite{xie2023dsir} selects pretraining data by importance resampling against a target distribution.
D4~\cite{tirumala2023d4} combines deduplication with diversification to reduce redundancy, and DoReMi~\cite{xie2023doremi} learns domain weights via a proxy model to optimize downstream performance.
These methods operate on distributional properties of the corpus but do not estimate whether individual documents have undergone recursive generation.

The closest prior work is Drayson et al.~\cite{drayson2025}, who combined binary machine-generated text detection with stratified importance resampling (SIR) to filter synthetic content and prevent model collapse.
Their approach is a special case of our graduated filtering framework: when $\Kstar = 1$, ordinal depth estimation reduces to binary classification, and depth-aware curation degenerates to their SIR-based scheme.
We generalize this binary formulation to ordinal depth estimation, enabling finer-grained curation that preserves mildly contaminated text (depth~1, retaining most original signal) while removing deeply corrupted text (depth~$\geq 2$).
%% C3-NEUTRAL ALTERNATIVE (activate if exp-006 triggers Version B):
%% We generalize this binary formulation to ordinal depth estimation.
%% Our experiments show that binary filtering at the $\Kstar$ boundary
%% already captures the actionable depth signal; graduated weighting
%% provides no additional downstream benefit, confirming that Drayson
%% et al.'s binary approach is not a simplification but the optimal
%% strategy given the information structure of recursive generation
%% (Section~\ref{sec:graduated-filtering}).
Recent work demonstrates that external verification can prevent model collapse during recursive training~\citep{feng2025beyond}.
Yi et al.~\cite{yi2025escaping} formalize verifier-guided retraining and show that verification effectiveness is bounded by the verifier's knowledge; our $\Kstar$ can inform such verifiers by delineating the depth frontier below which quality discrimination remains feasible, positioning depth estimation as a natural verification signal for data curation.
Amin et al.~\cite{amin2025escaping} demonstrated that even weak quality signals suffice to escape model collapse when applied iteratively, suggesting that approximate depth estimates beyond $\Kempirical$ may remain practically useful.
Gambetta et al.~\cite{gambetta2025surplexity} proposed surplexity as a text quality metric correlated with generative degradation, though without explicit depth calibration.

\paragraph{Watermarking and Provenance.}
An alternative approach embeds identifiers at generation time.
Kirchenbauer et al.~\cite{kirchenbauer2023watermark} proposed statistical watermarking for LLM outputs by partitioning the vocabulary into green and red token lists conditioned on preceding context.
Watermarking is complementary to depth estimation: it requires control over the generation process and cooperation from providers, whereas our method operates post-hoc on unwatermarked text.
The two approaches address different threat models---watermarking assumes a cooperative generator, while depth estimation targets uncontrolled settings where provenance metadata is unavailable.

1	\section{Introduction}
2	\label{sec:introduction}
3	
4	Web-scale text corpora are increasingly contaminated by synthetic content that has itself been generated from earlier synthetic content.
5	Each pass through a language model constitutes a lossy channel: first-generation synthetic text retains much of the information structure of its human-written source, but within just two or three generations the output is qualitatively different---tail modes vanish, lexical diversity contracts, and surprisal distributions flatten~\cite{shumailov2024collapse, dohmatob2024model}.
6	This recursive degradation is not merely a theoretical concern; as synthetic text proliferates on the open web, training corpora inevitably ingest documents at varying generational depths, amplifying the risk of model collapse in downstream systems.
7	Yet the dominant paradigm in synthetic text detection treats all machine-generated text identically: a document is classified as human or synthetic, with no regard for how many rounds of recursive generation it has undergone.
8	This binary framing discards the generational depth dimension entirely.
9	
10	The gap cuts across three research communities.

25	The primary contribution is a systematic empirical characterization of $\Kempirical$ and its properties:

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Web-scale text corpora are increasingly contaminated by synthetic content that has itself been generated from earlier synthetic content.
Each pass through a language model constitutes a lossy channel: first-generation synthetic text retains much of the information structure of its human-written source, but within just two or three generations the output is qualitatively different---tail modes vanish, lexical diversity contracts, and surprisal distributions flatten~\cite{shumailov2024collapse, dohmatob2024model}.
This recursive degradation is not merely a theoretical concern; as synthetic text proliferates on the open web, training corpora inevitably ingest documents at varying generational depths, amplifying the risk of model collapse in downstream systems.
Yet the dominant paradigm in synthetic text detection treats all machine-generated text identically: a document is classified as human or synthetic, with no regard for how many rounds of recursive generation it has undergone.
This binary framing discards the generational depth dimension entirely.

The gap cuts across three research communities.
Binary detection methods---including DivEye~\cite{basani2026diveye}, Min-K\%++~\cite{zhang2024minkpp}, and CoDeC~\cite{zawalski2026codec}---achieve strong human-versus-machine separation but produce no depth estimate.
The model collapse literature provides macro-level characterizations of recursive degradation: Shumailov et al.~\cite{shumailov2024collapse} demonstrated irreversible tail loss, Alemohammad et al.~\cite{alemohammad2024selfconsuming} proved convergence to a fixed point, and Schaeffer et al.~\cite{schaeffer2025position} organized the field into a taxonomy of eight definitions---yet none of these works provides a tool for estimating the generational depth of an individual text.
Data selection methods such as DSIR~\cite{xie2023dsir}, D4~\cite{tirumala2023d4}, and DoReMi~\cite{xie2023doremi} perform distribution matching to improve corpus quality but ignore recursive depth altogether.
The closest prior work is Drayson et al.~\cite{drayson2025}, who combined binary machine-generated text detection with stratified importance resampling to prevent model collapse---but their approach remains fundamentally binary.
No existing method estimates how many rounds of recursive generation a text has undergone, nor quantifies the boundary beyond which such estimation becomes infeasible.

Recursive generation forms an iterated lossy channel; the Data Processing Inequality guarantees that the original signal degrades monotonically across generations, motivating the existence of a finite discrimination boundary $\Kstar$ beyond which adjacent generations become indistinguishable.
Markov chain convergence further implies that adjacent-generation distributions converge to a shared stationary distribution, so the classifier's task grows harder with each step.
Motivated by this theoretical structure, we set out to empirically measure $\Kempirical$---the maximum depth at which a classifier can reliably distinguish adjacent generations.
Our approach combines a 15-dimensional statistical feature pipeline---capturing surprisal moments, surprisal derivatives, vocabulary diversity, and frequency tail statistics---with an Ordinal Binary Decomposition (OBD) LightGBM classifier that respects the ordinal structure of depth.
We operationalize $\Kempirical$ as the deepest generation at which adjacent depths remain statistically distinguishable, with the bootstrap 95\% CI for pairwise $\auc$ exceeding an operational threshold $\theta = 0.60$ (formal definition in Section~\ref{sec:method}).
The choice of interpretable statistical features---rather than learned representations---is deliberate: it enables cross-generator transfer without retraining and permits attribution of discriminative power to specific text properties.

Our contributions are organized into two groups.
The primary contribution is a systematic empirical characterization of $\Kempirical$ and its properties:

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
  \item \textbf{$\Kempirical = 2$: a consistent boundary across all tested conditions.}
    Across 4 model-mode configurations and 4 decoding strategies (8 conditions total), all 1v2 bootstrap CI lower bounds exceed $\theta = 0.60$ and all 2v3 CI upper bounds fall below $\theta$, with permutation $p \leq 0.002$ for all boundary comparisons.
    The most marginal case is Qwen-continuation, where $\text{CI}_\text{lower} = 0.6015$.
    $\Kempirical = 2$ is thus established as a consistent discrimination boundary across all 8 tested conditions at the $\leq$1.5B scale.
    Higher decoding entropy increases signal strength ($\auc_{1,2}$: $0.69$ greedy $\to$ $0.70$ at $T{=}1.2$) but does not shift the boundary.

  \item \textbf{Cross-model transfer.}
    Classifiers trained on one continuation-mode model and evaluated on another retain 80--92\% of within-model accuracy (Pythia$\leftrightarrow$OLMo: 90--92\%).
    At the 0v1 boundary, cross-model $\auc$ exceeds 0.96 across all tested model pairs.
    Transfer retention of 80--92\% suggests a large text-intrinsic component of the depth signal, rather than generator-specific artifacts.

  \item \textbf{Degradation ordering consistency.}
    Single-feature $\auc$ rankings are highly correlated across continuation-mode models (Spearman $\rho \geq 0.85$), with the same top features---\texttt{surp\_d1\_std}, \texttt{surp\_std}, \texttt{surp\_d2\_std}---appearing across all three families.
    This shared ordering suggests a common degradation mechanism: each generation step smooths the token-level surprisal landscape.
    A limitation is that depth-pair-level agreement weakens ($\tau \approx 0.37$ at 1v2), indicating that individual feature contributions at the boundary vary across models.

  \item \textbf{Generation mode analysis.}
    Within Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, rewrite mode yields 1v2 $\auc = 0.6955$ versus continuation's $0.6112$ ($\Delta = +8.4$\,pp), but rewrite-trained classifiers transfer poorly across models (61--63\% retention versus 80--92\% for continuation).
    Cross-mode transfer is asymmetric: continuation$\to$rewrite retains 89\% while rewrite$\to$continuation retains 82\%.
    Continuation mode is therefore recommended as the canonical condition for cross-model comparisons.
\end{enumerate}

\noindent As a secondary contribution, we investigate whether the coarse 3-class ordinal signal implied by $\Kempirical = 2$ enables \emph{graduated filtering}---depth-aware data curation that preserves mildly contaminated text (depth~1, retaining most original signal) while removing deeply corrupted text (depth~$\geq 2$)---and whether such filtering can improve upon binary approaches that discard all synthetic content indiscriminately (Section~\ref{sec:experiments}).

The remainder of this paper is organized as follows.
Section~\ref{sec:related_work} reviews related work.
Section~\ref{sec:method} describes the method.
Section~\ref{sec:experiments} presents experimental results.
Section~\ref{sec:discussion} discusses implications and limitations.
Section~\ref{sec:conclusion} concludes.

109	2. **"只是 feature engineering + off-the-shelf classifier，方法贡献弱"** → 贡献在 problem formulation + empirical characterization（首次测量 K*）+ 理论框架（DPI）+ universality 发现，不是分类器本身

112	5. **"同模型做生成和 surprisal 计算有 bias"** → **exp-013 直接反驳**：Pythia↔OLMo 90-92% accuracy retention，0v1 transfer AUC > 0.96。Depth signal 主要编码在文本而非 model self-familiarity
113	6. **"为什么不用 learned representations"** → **exp-015 直接回应**：frozen LLM embeddings + MLP probe 达到 K*=3（vs 15D K*=2），揭示 representation-dependent hierarchy: K*_theory ≥ K*_neural ≥ K*_15D。Hand-crafted 15D features 的优势在于 model-free transferability（80-92% cross-model retention）、可解释性（支持 degradation ordering 分析）、实用可部署性。Neural representations 多辨别 1 个深度级别但代价是 model dependence + ~100x 计算开销。这一 tradeoff 证明 15D features 是 practical choice，同时表明 theoretical boundary 延伸至 K*=2 之上
114	7. **"Graduated filtering 没和 data selection methods 比"** → exp-006 包含 DSIR baseline + α sensitivity sweep
115	8. **"Decoding strategy 只测了 4 种，coverage 不够"** → 覆盖了实践中最常见的 decoding 配置（greedy, nucleus sampling, temperature scaling high/low）；4/4 完全一致强化 universality claim；extreme decoding（top-k=1 之外的 pathological 配置）留作 future work
116	9. **"为什么不直接用 LLM 做 depth estimation"** → **exp-011 直接反驳**：GPT-5.5 和 Claude Opus 4.6 在 500 样本 zero-shot 5-class depth 分类上仅 33.1-33.2% accuracy（MAE ~1.1），低于 OBD 15-feature LightGBM 的 38.6%。二者 binary detection 均 ~88%，说明 LLM 能区分 human vs synthetic 但无法估计递归深度。depth estimation 是非平凡任务，需要专用特征工程
117	
118	## Venue Fit
119	
120	- EMNLP 2026 special theme 明确呼吁 data contamination, synthetic data feedback loops, data governance 方向的工作
121	- 2+1 claim 结构：C1' 是 comprehensive characterization study with universality finding，C3 是 practical application，generation mode analysis 增加深度
122	- Universality narrative 比 controllability 更有 impact：从 "K* depends on X, Y, Z" 升级为 "K*=2 is a universal boundary"，审稿人更容易记住和传播
123	- 风险：universality claim 在 ≤1.5B 规模下的外推性是最大攻击面 → 论文中 scope 明确、limitation 诚实、DPI 理论支撑泛化的合理性

# Paper Framing — gen-depth-contamination

## Target Venue
- Primary: EMNLP 2026 Main (ARR submission May 25, 2026)
- Fallback: EMNLP 2026 Findings
- Backup: AAAI 2027 (abstract July 25, paper August 1)

## Canonical Experimental Condition

**Continuation mode 是 cross-model 结论的基础。**

> "We evaluate both generation modes because real-world recursive contamination can arise from either. Our analysis reveals generation mode as a significant confound, leading us to recommend continuation mode as the canonical condition for cross-model comparisons."

| Condition | Pythia↔OLMo | Qwen↔others | 论文定位 |
|-----------|-------------|-------------|---------|
| Continuation | 90-92% retention | 80-85% retention | **主实验条件** — cross-model claims 的基础 |
| Rewrite (instruction) | N/A | 61-63% retention | **upper bound with mode-specific confound** — 仅作 ablation |

**原则**：
- C1' 的跨模型 claim 必须基于 continuation mode 数据
- Rewrite mode 的高 AUC (0.6957 vs cont 0.6114) 是 mode-specific signal amplification，不能作为泛化性证据
- mvp-001 (Qwen-rewrite) 定位为 "pilot study demonstrating feasibility"，后续用 continuation mode rigorously validate
- cont→rw 89% vs rw→cont 82% 不对称性 → continuation features 是 rewrite 的通用子集

## Core Claims (2+1 结构, D012)

### Primary: C1' (K* Characterization)
首次系统测量递归合成文本的 generational discrimination boundary K*，并揭示其 universality。

DPI 理论证明有限 K*_theory 必然存在（信息论 impossibility boundary）；我们首次在受控实验中测量 K*_empirical，它提供 K*_theory 的保守下界。通过 8 条件实验矩阵（4 model-mode configurations + 4 decoding strategies）系统表征 K*_empirical 的行为，发现 K*=2 在所有 8 个测试条件下保持不变，展现出跨模型架构、跨解码策略、跨生成模式的 universality。

**子组件：**

**(a) K*=2 universality across architectures, generation modes, and decoding strategies**
> **4/4 model-mode configurations 与 4/4 decoding strategies 全部 K*=2：**
>
> *Model × mode (exp-007):*
> | Model | AUC 1v2 | 95% CI | CI lower > 0.60? |
> |-------|---------|--------|-----------------|
> | Qwen-rewrite | 0.6955 | [0.6859, 0.7041] | ✅ (+8.6pp) |
> | Pythia-1.4B | 0.6539 | [0.6454, 0.6630] | ✅ (+4.5pp) |
> | OLMo-1B | 0.6145 | [0.6045, 0.6247] | ✅ (+0.45pp) |
> | Qwen-cont | 0.6112 | [0.6015, 0.6213] | ✅ (+0.15pp, 最边缘) |
>
> *Decoding strategy invariance (exp-003):*
> | Decoding | AUC 1v2 | K* |
> |----------|---------|-----|
> | greedy | 0.6893 | 2 |
> | nucleus p=0.9 | 0.6866 | 2 |
> | temp=0.7 | 0.6887 | 2 |
> | temp=1.2 | 0.7039 | 2 |
>
> - 全部 1v2 CI lower > 0.60, 全部 2v3 CI upper < 0.60, 全部 permutation p < 0.002
> - 4 decoding strategies 的 AUC 1v2 range [0.6866, 0.7039]，K* 完全不变
> - K*=2 在所有 8 个测试条件下保持不变（4 model-mode configurations + 4 decoding strategies）
> - ⚠️ θ-sensitivity: θ=0.60 下 4/4 K*=2；θ=0.70 下仅 Config4-T12 K*=2（1v2=0.7039 仅超 0.70 阈值 0.004），其余 3 config K*=1。论文以 θ=0.60 为主结论，θ=0.70 边界效应作 footnote
> - ⚠️ 特征排序分化: K* 跨 config 稳定，但特征重要性排序不完全一致——Greedy vs T1.2 Spearman=0.53, p=0.041（Bonferroni 校正后阈值 0.0083，不显著）。论文中措辞应为 "suggestive" 而非确定性结论。Config4-T12 正确 top-3 features: hapax_ratio, ttr, surp_skew（非 freq_entropy）
> - ⚠️ K*=2 边缘性双端注意: Qwen-cont 1v2 CI lower=0.6015（+0.15pp 高于 θ）+ Qwen-rw 2v3 CI upper=0.5991（-0.09pp 低于 θ），K*=2 边界在两端都极边缘。Discussion/Limitations 需同时提及
> - Paper 可写："K*=2 is established as a consistent discrimination boundary across all 8 tested conditions (4 model-mode configurations and 4 decoding strategies; bootstrap 95% CI for AUC₁ᵥ₂ > 0.60; AUC₂ᵥ₃ CI upper < 0.60), suggesting universality beyond the ≤1.5B scale studied."
> - ⚠️ 措辞策略（D017 Reviewer 评估）：分两层——"established as consistent" 用确定性语言（8/8 有统计检验支撑），"suggesting universality beyond" 对外推 hedging。不升级为 "establishing universal"——3 模型 ≤1.5B 会引发审稿人质疑消耗 rebuttal 预算
> - ⚠️ C1' 子组件定位：呈现为"对同一 claim 的 4 个 evidence 维度"而非 4 个独立 finding。§4 标题用 "K* Characterization"，每个子节开头显式回答一个 reviewer concern，子节间用 transitional sentences 链接

**(b) Cross-model transfer**
> - Pythia↔OLMo 90-92% accuracy retention → K*=2 不是 model self-familiarity artifact
> - 0v1 AUC > 0.96 across all transfer pairs → binary contamination signal 完全跨模型可迁移
> - 1v2+ transfer 取决于模型族相似度 → 与 K*=2 完美一致（K* 之上分辨力本就微弱）
> - transfer retention 80-92% suggests depth signal has a large text-intrinsic component（不量化具体比例，因 transfer accuracy retention ≠ 信号分解）
> - ⚠️ 数值精度：Pythia→OLMo 91.6%, OLMo→Pythia 90.3%，范围 90-92%（非 91-92%）；Qwen-cont↔Pythia 84.7%/85.2%，范围 84-85%（非 83-85%）

**(c) Degradation ordering consistency**
> - Spearman ρ ≥ 0.85 on single-feature AUC ranking（mode-controlled, continuation）
> - Top discriminative features shared: surp_d1_std, surp_std, surp_d2_std
> - Limitation: depth-pair level 一致性在 1v2 处较弱（τ~0.37）
> - Metric: single-feature AUC ranking（model-free, not LightGBM split count）

**(e) Representation dependence of K* (§4.x Neural Probe / §5.x Discussion)**
> - exp-015: frozen Qwen-1.5B embeddings (1536-dim) + MLP probe → K*(neural)=3 on Qwen-cont（2v3 AUC=0.6195, fold range [0.6052, 0.6323]）
> - K* hierarchy: K*_theory ≥ K*_neural ≥ K*_15D，证明 K* 是表示复杂度的函数，K*_15D=2 是操作下界而非信息论极限
> - Interpretability–discriminability tradeoff: 15D features（K*=2, model-free, interpretable, deployable）vs neural probe（K*=3, model-dependent, opaque, 100x+ compute）
> - ⚠️ 当前仅 Qwen-cont 1 个数据集（Pythia/OLMo 待重跑）。若 Pythia/OLMo K*_neural=2 → self-familiarity 效应（Qwen embeddings 对 Qwen 生成文本更敏感），反而加强 15D model-free features 的定位
> - ⚠️ 2v3 边界极度边缘（fold 2 仅 +0.52pp 超 θ），需 bootstrap CI + permutation test 统计确认（重跑脚本已含）
> - 论文定位：**深化 K* characterization**（不推翻 K*=2 headline）。Headline 保持 "K*_empirical=2 under 15D hand-crafted features"，新增子结论 "K*_neural=3 demonstrates representation-dependent boundary"
> - Discussion 结构：§5.1 现有内容保留 + §5.1bis "Representation Dependence of K*" 独立子节（积极发现，非 limitation）
> - 预防审稿人 "why bury the stronger result?"：K*_15D=2 是 practical/deployable boundary，K*_neural=3 是 theoretical exploration，两者服务不同目的

**(d) Generation mode analysis (§4.x Analysis subsection)**
> - Signal strength: rewrite AUC 1v2=0.6957 vs continuation 0.6114（Δ=+8.4pp）
> - Transferability: continuation 80-92% retention vs rewrite 61-63%
> - Feature subset: cont→rw 89% > rw→cont 82% → continuation features 是 rewrite 的通用子集
> - Interpretation: rewrite mode 的 instruction-following 引入 mode-specific style artifacts，放大 depth signal 但降低跨模型泛化性
> - 论文定位：Analysis subsection（"How does generation mode affect depth estimation?"），不是独立 claim

### Secondary: C3 (Graduated Filtering)
即使在 K*=2 的粗粒度 ordinal signal（human/gen-1/gen-2+ 三级）下，K*-aware graduated filtering 仍优于 binary filtering，因为 ordinal signal 在阈值附近提供更 calibrated 的质量估计。

### Supporting Analysis: Canonical Condition Selection
Generation mode 是 depth estimation 的显著混淆变量。Methodology 段落阐述 continuation mode 作为 canonical condition 的选择及理由（不作为独立 claim）。

## Story Spine

- **Problem**: Web 数据正被多代递归合成文本污染。当前检测方法将合成文本视为 binary 类别（real vs synthetic），但质量随代际深度非线性退化——首代合成文本与四代合成文本的质量差异巨大却被忽视。
- **Existing approaches & gaps**: Binary detectors (DivEye, Min-K%++) 不区分代际；model collapse 文献 (Shumailov et al., Alemohammad et al. 2024, Dohmatob et al. 2024) 描述宏观现象但不提供检测工具；data selection methods (DSIR, D4, DoReMi) 做分布匹配但不估计递归深度；Drayson et al. (2025) 将 binary MGT detection 应用于 importance resampling 以防止 model collapse，是目前最接近的工作。然而这些方法均做二值判断，**不估计文本经历了多少轮递归生成，也不量化辨别能力的饱和边界。**
- **Our framing**: 将递归生成建模为 iterated lossy channel，从信息论（DPI）推导出 K* 的必然存在。K* 是首次系统测量的 operational quantity——它告诉数据策展者"在什么深度以下，depth-aware curation 比 binary detection 更有价值"。通过 8 条件实验矩阵（4 model-mode configurations + 4 decoding strategies）系统表征 K*，揭示其 universality：**K*=2 在所有测试条件下不变**，表明递归生成存在一个与具体模型架构和解码策略无关的 universal discrimination boundary。这一发现为数据治理提供 actionable guidance——depth-aware filtering 在 K* 以内有效，且无需针对不同模型或解码配置分别调优。
- **Headline result template**: "Recursive generation has a universal discrimination boundary at K*=2: invariant across 4 model-mode configurations and 4 decoding strategies (8 conditions total) at ≤1.5B scale, with cross-model transfer retention of 80-92% confirming depth features are largely text-intrinsic. Even this coarse 3-class signal yields X% improvement over binary filtering on MMLU/HellaSwag."

## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns & Responses

1. **"Universality claim 只基于 ≤1.5B 模型，能推广到更大模型吗？"** → 这是最大 limitation，论文明确标注 "at ≤1.5B scale"；但 (i) universality 在 4 个不同架构族（GPT-2 style, Pythia, OLMo, Qwen）间已成立，说明不是单一架构的 artifact；(ii) DPI 理论保证 K*_theory 对任意规模模型存在，实证 K*_empirical 在更大模型上可能更大（信号更丰富）也可能不变（lossy channel 特性稳定），这是重要的 future work
2. **"只是 feature engineering + off-the-shelf classifier，方法贡献弱"** → 贡献在 problem formulation + empirical characterization（首次测量 K*）+ 理论框架（DPI）+ universality 发现，不是分类器本身
3. **"Prompt-chain 不代表真实世界递归污染"** → retrain-chain ecological validity check 作为补充；prompt-chain 是 controlled experiment 的标准方法
4. **"K*=2 太浅，graduated filtering 收益有限"** → universality 恰好说明这是 fundamental boundary 而非实验 artifact；即使 K*=2，3-class（human/gen-1/gen-2+）比 binary 在阈值附近更 calibrated（exp-006）；K* 的 universality 意味着实践者无需为每个模型/解码配置单独标定阈值
5. **"同模型做生成和 surprisal 计算有 bias"** → **exp-013 直接反驳**：Pythia↔OLMo 90-92% accuracy retention，0v1 transfer AUC > 0.96。Depth signal 主要编码在文本而非 model self-familiarity
6. **"为什么不用 learned representations"** → **exp-015 直接回应**：frozen LLM embeddings + MLP probe 达到 K*=3（vs 15D K*=2），揭示 representation-dependent hierarchy: K*_theory ≥ K*_neural ≥ K*_15D。Hand-crafted 15D features 的优势在于 model-free transferability（80-92% cross-model retention）、可解释性（支持 degradation ordering 分析）、实用可部署性。Neural representations 多辨别 1 个深度级别但代价是 model dependence + ~100x 计算开销。这一 tradeoff 证明 15D features 是 practical choice，同时表明 theoretical boundary 延伸至 K*=2 之上
7. **"Graduated filtering 没和 data selection methods 比"** → exp-006 包含 DSIR baseline + α sensitivity sweep
8. **"Decoding strategy 只测了 4 种，coverage 不够"** → 覆盖了实践中最常见的 decoding 配置（greedy, nucleus sampling, temperature scaling high/low）；4/4 完全一致强化 universality claim；extreme decoding（top-k=1 之外的 pathological 配置）留作 future work
9. **"为什么不直接用 LLM 做 depth estimation"** → **exp-011 直接反驳**：GPT-5.5 和 Claude Opus 4.6 在 500 样本 zero-shot 5-class depth 分类上仅 33.1-33.2% accuracy（MAE ~1.1），低于 OBD 15-feature LightGBM 的 38.6%。二者 binary detection 均 ~88%，说明 LLM 能区分 human vs synthetic 但无法估计递归深度。depth estimation 是非平凡任务，需要专用特征工程

## Venue Fit

- EMNLP 2026 special theme 明确呼吁 data contamination, synthetic data feedback loops, data governance 方向的工作
- 2+1 claim 结构：C1' 是 comprehensive characterization study with universality finding，C3 是 practical application，generation mode analysis 增加深度
- Universality narrative 比 controllability 更有 impact：从 "K* depends on X, Y, Z" 升级为 "K*=2 is a universal boundary"，审稿人更容易记住和传播
- 风险：universality claim 在 ≤1.5B 规模下的外推性是最大攻击面 → 论文中 scope 明确、limitation 诚实、DPI 理论支撑泛化的合理性
